name: Angath
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Unterinntal with a picturesque old town center and direct access to the hiking trails of the Kaisergebirge.
beschreibung:
Overview

Angath is situated at an elevation of 500 meters on the northern bank of the Inn River in the Lower Inn Valley of Tyrol, directly opposite the transport and commercial hub of Wörgl. Located in the district of Kufstein and forming part of the Hohe Salve holiday region in the Kitzbühel Alps, the municipality covers roughly 3.5 square kilometers and is home to about 1,000 residents. Despite its proximity to bustling Wörgl, Angath has preserved its peaceful village atmosphere, characterized by lush river meadows, traditional farmhouses, and views toward the Kaiser Mountains and the Kitzbühel Alps. The Inn River meanders gracefully around the village, bordered by the international Inn Cycle Path.

History

Angath's heritage is intimately connected to river navigation: it was first documented in 1188 as Anegathę in the records of Raitenhaslach Monastery, a name derived from Old High German anegaht, meaning river embankment. In the 15th and 16th centuries, Angath grew into one of the three primary river ports of Tyrol alongside Hall and Langkampfen, serving as the central shipyard for the region. Here, traditional wooden barges were built to transport silver from Schwaz, salt from Hall, and timber down the Danube all the way to Vienna. Historical ties to Frauenchiemsee Abbey dating to 1315 are commemorated in the municipal coat of arms, which depicts a water lily leaf alongside two crossed boat oars.

Getting There

Reaching Angath is exceptionally straightforward thanks to adjacent transport links: Wörgl Central Station, a major stop for Railjet, ICE, and Nightjet trains with direct connections from Vienna, Munich, Zurich, and Innsbruck, is located just two kilometers away. From the station, VVT regional buses connect to Angath, or visitors can walk or cycle across the footbridge over the Inn in minutes. Motorists take the Inntal Motorway A12 to exits Wörgl-Ost or Kirchbichl, reaching the village in under five minutes via the L212 road. Cyclists can pedal directly along the Inn Cycle Path (R2).

Tips

The centerpiece of the village is the Baroque Holy Spirit Parish Church, constructed in 1746–1747 and attributed to noted Tyrolean master builder Jakob Singer, featuring elegant barrel vaulting and ornate Rococo altars. Cycling along the scenic Inn River loop on the Inn Cycle Path provides wonderful leisure for families. Nearby highlights include the Hundalm Ice Cave on Mount Angerberg—Tyrol's only publicly accessible ice and stalactite cave at 1,520 meters—and the dramatic pilgrimage fortress of Mariastein just four kilometers away. Winter enthusiasts can access the lifts of SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser – Brixental in under fifteen minutes.
